criteria: In paginate.py, `page_count(total_items, per_page)` returns the number of pages needed: 20 items at 10 per page is 2 pages, 21 items is 3 pages, and zero items is 1 page, because the site always shows one page.

In paginate.py, `page_slice(total_items, per_page, page)` returns `(start, end)`, the index of the first item on the page and one past the last item, so that `items[start:end]` is the page. Pages are numbered from 1, the last page may be short, and a page below 1 or above `page_count` raises `ValueError`.

In paginate.py, `page_window(total_items, per_page, page, size=5)` returns the list of page numbers to show in the pager, following these rules. It lists `size` consecutive page numbers, or all pages when there are fewer than `size`. The current page is in the middle when it can be. With an even `size` the extra page goes after the current one, so `size=4` around page 5 of 10 is `[4, 5, 6, 7]`. Near the first or the last page the window is shifted to stay inside 1 to `page_count` and keeps its full length, so page 10 of 10 with `size=5` is `[6, 7, 8, 9, 10]`. A page below 1 or above `page_count`, and a `size` below 1, raise `ValueError`.
In all three functions, `page_count`, `page_slice` and `page_window`, a `per_page` below 1 and a `total_items` below 0 raise `ValueError`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
